title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
why_read: BioScore offers a label-free way to benchmark pathology image encoders against ground-truth cell biology using spatial transcriptomics, which is a more principled evaluation than task accuracy alone.
analysis: Most benchmarks for pathology foundation models measure downstream task performance, such as tumour classification accuracy, without asking whether the model actually learned meaningful biology. BioScore addresses this by using spatial transcriptomics — which maps gene expression across tissue at spatial resolution — as a reference for what cell types are present and where. A sparse autoencoder decomposes the model's patch embeddings into interpretable features, and those features are tested for alignment with 52 cell identities defined by marker genes. The approach is fully unsupervised, needs no manually labelled data, and ranks eight pathology models in a way that agrees with supervised probing, while also revealing which specific cell types each model captures or misses.
